problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2-x-y,\,y(0)=1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the modified Euler method. Complete the first row of the table below, given that the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{4}.$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $1$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{5}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | {{field-1}} |

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}{y}^{2}-x,\,y(0)=1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the modified Euler method. Complete the first row of the table below, given that the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{5}.$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $-\frac{4}{25}$ | {{field-1}} |
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the modified Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where ${y}_{p}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is the initially predicted slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})=(x+Δx,y+Δ{y}_{p}).$

We compute $Δy$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0+(-\frac{4}{25}))\cdot \frac{1}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(-\frac{4}{25}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{125}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed first row is as given below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $-\frac{4}{25}$ | $-\frac{2}{125}$ |
